blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 3

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27-40, which are based on Reading Passage 3 below.

On art and artists

A

There really is no such thing as art, only artists. Once these were people who took coloured earth and roughed out the forms of a bison on the wall of a cave; today some buy their paints, and others design posters for hoardings; they did and do many other things. There is no harm in calling all these activities art as long as we keep in mind that such a word may mean very different things in different times and places, and as long as we realize that Art with a capital A has no existence: it has become something of an obsession. You may crush an artist by telling him that what he has just done may be quite good in its own way, only it is not true art.

B

Actually, I do not think that there are any wrong reasons for liking a statue or a picture. We may like a painting of a village scene because it reminds us of home. There is nothing wrong with that. All of us, when we see a painting, are bound to be reminded of a hundred-and-one things which influence our likes and dislikes. As long as these memories help us to enjoy what we see, we need not worry.

C

It is only when some irrelevant memory makes us prejudiced, when we instinctively turn away from a magnificent picture of an alpine scene because we dislike climbing, that we should search our mind for the reason for the aversion which spoils a pleasure we might otherwise have had. There are wrong reasons for disliking a work of art.

D

Most people like to see in pictures what they would also like to see in reality. This is quite a natural preference. We all like beauty in nature, and are grateful to the artists who have preserved it in their works. Nor would these artists themselves have rebuffed us for our taste. When the great Flemish painter Rubens made a drawing of his young son, he was surely proud of his good looks, and wanted us, too, to delight in the child's appearance. But this bias for the pretty and engaging subject is apt to become a stumbling block if it leads us to reject works which represent a less appealing subject.

E

The great German painter Durer certainly drew his mother with as much devotion and love as Rubens felt for his child. His truthful study of old age may give us a shock which makes us turn away from it - and yet, if we fight against that first reaction we may be richly rewarded. For Durer's drawing in its tremendous sincerity is a great work. The beauty of a picture does not really lie in the beauty of its subject matter. The trouble about beauty is that tastes and standards of what is beautiful vary so much.

F

What is true of beauty is also true of facial expression. In fact, it is often the expression of a figure in the painting which makes us like or loathe the work. Some people like an expression - perhaps of suffering or of compassion - which they can readily understand, and which therefore moves them profoundly. But we should not, for that reason, turn away from works whose expression is perhaps less easy to understand. Often we must first learn to know the artist's methods of drawing to understand the feelings he or she wishes to portray, and may even come to prefer works of art in which expression is not obvious. Just as some of us would rather people use few words and gestures and leave something to be guessed, so some of us would rather look at paintings or sculptures which are open to interpretation.

G

But here newcomers to art are often brought up against another difficulty. They want to admire the artist's skill in representing the things they see. What they like best are paintings which 'look real'. This is an important consideration, and the patience and skill which go into the faithful rendering of the visible world are indeed to be admired. Great artists of the past have devoted much labour to works in which every tiny detail is carefully recorded. Durer's watercolour study of a hare is one of the most famous examples of this loving patience. But who would say that Rembrandt's drawing of an elephant is necessarily less good because it shows fewer details? Indeed Rembrandt gave us the feel of the elephant's wrinkly skin with just a few lines of his chalk.

H

If we find fault with the accuracy of a picture, we must remember that artists may have their reasons for changing the appearance of what they see. We should also never condemn a work for being incorrectly drawn unless we are quite sure that we are right and the painter is wrong. We have a curious habit of thinking that nature must always look like the pictures we are accustomed to. For generations, paintings showed horses galloping with outstretched legs in full flight through the air, and we came to believe that this was indeed how they moved. It was only the development of photography which proved that horses simply do not gallop in that way. And yet, when painters began to apply this new discovery, and painted horses moving as they actually do, everyone complained that their pictures looked wrong.

Questions 31-36

Look at the following statements (Questions 31-36) and the list of subjects below.

Match each statement with the correct subject, A-G.

Write the correct letter, A-G, in boxes 31-36 on your answer sheet.

31 The artist clearly hoped that we would share his admiration of this subject.

32 The artist aims to give a general impression of this subject rather than a detailed one.

33 Someone's personal experience may make them consider a painting of this subject unpleasant.

34 The way in which this subject was once portrayed was factually wrong.

35 The painting is well known for the effort the artist put into creating a very accurate picture of this subject.

36 People may like a painting of this subject for a reason that is external to the painting.

List of Subjects
A village scene
B alpine scene
C Rubens's son
D Durer's mother
E hare
F elephant
G horses

Questions 37-40

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

Beauty and expression

Differences in tastes and standards of beauty make it difficult to judge a painting. Durer's painting of his mother is considered significant because it is a representation of her age and situation. However, we may need to overcome an initial reaction of when we see it. In order to judge the facial expressions of people portrayed in a painting, we need to become familiar with the methods that the artist has used when creating the painting. passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 实际上没有艺术这种东西，只有艺术家。曾经，这些人用彩色泥土在洞穴墙壁上粗略勾勒出野牛的形状；今天，有些人购买颜料，还有些人为广告牌设计海报；他们做了并将继续做许多其他事情。只要记住这个词在不同时代和地点可能意味着非常不同的事物，只要我们意识到大写的“Art”并不存在，那么将所有这些活动称为艺术并无害处：它已成为一种执念。如果你告诉一位艺术家，他刚刚完成的作品可能在其自身方式上相当不错，只是不是真正的艺术，你可能会摧毁他。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 实际上，我认为喜欢一座雕像或一幅画没有任何错误的理由。我们可能喜欢一幅乡村风景画，因为它让我们想起家乡。这没有任何问题。当我们看到一幅画时，所有人都会被提醒一百零一件事物，这些事物影响着我们的好恶。只要这些记忆有助于我们欣赏所看到的东西，我们就不必担心。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 只有当某些无关的记忆使我们产生偏见时，比如因为我们不喜欢攀岩而本能地转身离开一幅壮丽的阿尔卑斯山风景画，我们才应该审视自己的内心，寻找破坏我们本可能获得的愉悦的反感原因。存在不喜欢一件艺术作品的错误理由。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 大多数人喜欢在画中看到他们在现实中也想看到的东西。这是一种相当自然的偏好。我们都喜欢大自然中的美，并感谢艺术家们在作品中保存了它。这些艺术家本身也不会因我们的品味而拒绝我们。当伟大的佛兰德斯画家鲁本斯为他的小儿子画一幅素描时，他肯定为孩子的英俊感到骄傲，并希望我们也为孩子的容貌感到欣喜。但是，如果对漂亮和迷人主题的偏好导致我们拒绝表现不那么吸引人的主题的作品，那么这种偏好就会成为绊脚石。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 伟大的德国画家丢勒画他的母亲时，无疑倾注了与鲁本斯对孩子一样的深情和爱意。他对老年真实的描绘可能会给我们一种震惊，使我们转身离开 —— 然而，如果我们与这种第一反应抗争，我们可能会得到丰厚的回报。因为丢勒的画作以其巨大的真诚而成为一件伟大的作品。一幅画的美并不真正在于其主题的美。关于美的问题是，品味和美的标准变化如此之大。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 关于美的事物同样适用于面部表情。事实上，往往是画中人物的表情使我们喜欢或厌恶这件作品。有些人喜欢一种表情 —— 也许是痛苦或同情 —— 他们可以轻松理解，因此深受感动。但我们不应因此转身离开那些表情可能不太容易理解的作品。通常，我们必须首先了解艺术家的绘画方法，才能理解他或她想要描绘的情感，甚至可能更喜欢那些表情不明显的艺术作品。就像我们中有些人宁愿人们少用言语和手势，留一些让人猜测的东西一样，我们中有些人宁愿看那些开放解读的绘画或雕塑。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 但在这里，艺术新手常常遇到另一个困难。他们想欣赏艺术家在描绘他们所看到的事物方面的技能。他们最喜欢的是“看起来真实”的画作。这是一个重要的考虑因素，投入到忠实再现可见世界的耐心和技巧确实值得钦佩。过去的伟大艺术家们为每一件微小细节都被仔细记录的作品投入了大量劳动。丢勒的野兔水彩研究是这种充满爱心的耐心的最著名例子之一。但谁会说伦勃朗的大象素描因为显示较少的细节就必然差一些呢？事实上，伦勃朗仅用几笔粉笔就给了我们大象皱巴巴皮肤的感觉。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph H
passageNotes.text: 如果我们对一幅画的准确性有意见，我们必须记住，艺术家可能有他们改变所看到事物外观的理由。我们也绝不应因一幅画得不正确而谴责一件作品，除非我们完全确定我们是对的而画家是错的。我们有一种奇怪的习惯，认为自然必须看起来像我们习惯的画作。几代人以来，画作展示了马匹在空中伸展双腿全速奔跑，我们开始相信这确实是它们移动的方式。直到摄影的发展才证明马匹根本不是那样奔跑的。然而，当画家们开始应用这一新发现，并按照马匹实际移动的方式绘画时，每个人都抱怨他们的画看起来不对。

items.text:
（1）题目 27：a comparison between people's preferences towards language and art
题目翻译：人们对语言和艺术的偏好之间的比较
答案：F
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Just as some of us would rather people use few words and gestures and leave something to be guessed, so some of us would rather look at paintings or sculptures which are open to interpretation”。作者将人们对语言（少用言语和手势）的偏好与对艺术（开放解读的绘画或雕塑）的偏好进行比较，因此答案为 F。

（2）题目 28：why people may have misunderstood how a certain animal moves
题目翻译：为什么人们可能误解了某种动物的移动方式
答案：H
解析：定位 Paragraph H 中 “For generations, paintings showed horses galloping with outstretched legs in full flight through the air, and we came to believe that this was indeed how they moved. It was only the development of photography which proved that horses simply do not gallop in that way”。几代人以来，人们根据画作相信马匹伸展双腿奔跑，直到摄影才证明这不是马匹实际的移动方式，因此答案为 H。

（3）题目 29：a contrast between the techniques used in two pictures
题目翻译：两幅画作中使用的技术对比
答案：G
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “Durer's watercolour study of a hare is one of the most famous examples of this loving patience. But who would say that Rembrandt's drawing of an elephant is necessarily less good because it shows fewer details?”。作者对比了丢勒的野兔水彩（详细记录）和伦勃朗的大象素描（较少细节），因此答案为 G。

（4）题目 30：a possible negative effect of using the term 'art'
题目翻译：使用“艺术”一词可能产生的负面影响
答案：A
解析：定位 Paragraph A 中 “You may crush an artist by telling him that what he has just done may be quite good in its own way, only it is not true art”。告诉艺术家作品不是“真正的艺术”可能会摧毁他，这是使用“艺术”一词的负面影响，因此答案为 A。

items.text:
（1）题目 31：The artist clearly hoped that we would share his admiration of this subject.
题目翻译：艺术家显然希望我们分享他对这个主题的赞赏。
答案：C（Rubens's son）
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “When the great Flemish painter Rubens made a drawing of his young son, he was surely proud of his good looks, and wanted us, too, to delight in the child's appearance”。鲁本斯为儿子作画时，希望我们也为孩子的容貌感到欣喜，即希望我们分享他的赞赏，因此答案为 C。

（2）题目 32：The artist aims to give a general impression of this subject rather than a detailed one.
题目翻译：艺术家旨在给出这个主题的总体印象，而非详细的描绘。
答案：F（elephant）
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “Rembrandt's drawing of an elephant is necessarily less good because it shows fewer details? Indeed Rembrandt gave us the feel of the elephant's wrinkly skin with just a few lines of his chalk”。伦勃朗的大象素描用几笔粉笔就给出了皮肤的感觉，即总体印象而非详细描绘，因此答案为 F。

（3）题目 33：Someone's personal experience may make them consider a painting of this subject unpleasant.
题目翻译：某人的个人经历可能使他认为这个主题的画作令人不快。
答案：B（alpine scene）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “when we instinctively turn away from a magnificent picture of an alpine scene because we dislike climbing”。如果我们不喜欢攀岩，可能会本能地转身离开一幅壮丽的阿尔卑斯山风景画，即个人经历使画作令人不快，因此答案为 B。

（4）题目 34：The way in which this subject was once portrayed was factually wrong.
题目翻译：这个主题曾经的描绘方式在事实上是错误的。
答案：G（horses）
解析：定位 Paragraph H 中 “For generations, paintings showed horses galloping with outstretched legs in full flight through the air, and we came to believe that this was indeed how they moved. It was only the development of photography which proved that horses simply do not gallop in that way”。马匹曾经的描绘方式（伸展双腿奔跑）被证明是错误的，因此答案为 G。

（5）题目 35：The painting is well known for the effort the artist put into creating a very accurate picture of this subject.
题目翻译：这幅画因艺术家为创作这个主题的非常准确的画面所付出的努力而闻名。
答案：E（hare）
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “Durer's watercolour study of a hare is one of the most famous examples of this loving patience”。丢勒的野兔水彩研究是这种充满爱心的耐心的最著名例子之一，即因准确描绘而闻名，因此答案为 E。

（6）题目 36：People may like a painting of this subject for a reason that is external to the painting.
题目翻译：人们可能因为画作之外的原因而喜欢这个主题的画作。
答案：A（village scene）
解析：定位 Paragraph B 中 “We may like a painting of a village scene because it reminds us of home”。我们可能喜欢一幅乡村风景画，因为它让我们想起家乡，这是画作之外的原因，因此答案为 A。

items.text:
（1）题目 37：Durer's painting of his mother is considered significant because it is a ______ representation of her age and situation.
题目翻译：丢勒母亲的画作被认为具有重要意义，因为它是对她年龄和处境的 ______ 描绘。
答案：truthful
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “His truthful study of old age may give us a shock which makes us turn away from it”。丢勒对老年的真实（truthful）描绘，因此答案为 truthful。

（2）题目 38：However, we may need to overcome an initial reaction of ______ when we see it.
题目翻译：然而，当我们看到它时，我们可能需要克服最初的 ______ 反应。
答案：shock
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “His truthful study of old age may give us a shock which makes us turn away from it”。丢勒的画作可能会给我们一种震惊（shock），使我们转身离开，因此答案为 shock。

（3）题目 39：While some of us are affected by the portrayal of a facial expression that we can ______ without much effort, others prefer expressions that require interpretation.
题目翻译：虽然我们中有些人会受到面部表情描绘的影响，这种表情我们可以毫不费力地 ______，但其他人更喜欢需要解读的表情。
答案：understand
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Some people like an expression - perhaps of suffering or of compassion - which they can readily understand”。有些人喜欢他们可以轻松理解（readily understand）的表情，因此答案为 understand。

（4）题目 40：While some of us are affected by the portrayal of a facial expression that we can understand without much effort, others prefer expressions that require ______.
题目翻译：虽然我们中有些人会受到面部表情描绘的影响，这种表情我们可以毫不费力地理解，但其他人更喜欢需要 ______ 的表情。
答案：interpretation
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “so some of us would rather look at paintings or sculptures which are open to interpretation”。我们中有些人宁愿看那些开放解读（interpretation）的绘画或雕塑，因此答案为 interpretation。

questionExplanations.text:
题目翻译：丢勒母亲的画作被认为具有重要意义，因为它是对她年龄和处境的 ______ 描绘。
答案：truthful
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “His truthful study of old age may give us a shock which makes us turn away from it”。丢勒对老年的真实（truthful）描绘，因此答案为 truthful。
题目翻译：然而，当我们看到它时，我们可能需要克服最初的 ______ 反应。
答案：shock
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “His truthful study of old age may give us a shock which makes us turn away from it”。丢勒的画作可能会给我们一种震惊（shock），使我们转身离开，因此答案为 shock。
题目翻译：虽然我们中有些人会受到面部表情描绘的影响，这种表情我们可以毫不费力地 ______，但其他人更喜欢需要解读的表情。
答案：understand
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Some people like an expression - perhaps of suffering or of compassion - which they can readily understand”。有些人喜欢他们可以轻松理解（readily understand）的表情，因此答案为 understand。
题目翻译：虽然我们中有些人会受到面部表情描绘的影响，这种表情我们可以毫不费力地理解，但其他人更喜欢需要 ______ 的表情。
答案：interpretation
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “so some of us would rather look at paintings or sculptures which are open to interpretation”。我们中有些人宁愿看那些开放解读（interpretation）的绘画或雕塑，因此答案为 interpretation。
